questions.question: Which constitutional body audits the accounts of the Union and states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Comptroller and Auditor General**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG)** is an independent authority established under **Article 148** of the Constitution of India.
 
• The CAG serves as the head of the **Indian Audit and Accounts Department** and acts as the **guardian of the public purse**, ensuring financial accountability of the executive to the Parliament.
 
• According to **Article 149**, the CAG audits all expenditure from the **Consolidated Fund of India**, the **Consolidated Fund of each State**, and the **Consolidated Fund of each Union Territory** having a Legislative Assembly.
 
• The CAG also audits all expenditure from the **Contingency Fund of India** and the **Public Account of India**, as well as the contingency fund and public account of each state.
 
• Under **Article 151**, the audit reports relating to the accounts of the Union are submitted to the **President**, who causes them to be laid before each **House of Parliament**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Finance Commission**:

 
 
• Established under **Article 280** of the Constitution, it is a quasi-judicial body that recommends the distribution of **tax proceeds** between the Union and the States and the principles governing **grants-in-aid**.
 
 
 
• **NITI Aayog**:
 
 
• Replacing the Planning Commission on **January 1, 2015**, it is a **non-constitutional** and **non-statutory** body serving as the premier policy **Think Tank** of the Government of India.
 
 
 
• **Union Public Service Commission (UPSC)**:
 
 
• A constitutional body established under **Articles 315 to 323** of Part XIV, responsible for conducting examinations for appointments to the **services of the Union**.

questions.question: Which type of emergency has never been proclaimed in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Financial Emergency**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Emergency Provisions** are contained in **Part XVIII** of the **Constitution of India**, spanning from **Article 352 to Article 360**.
 
• **Article 360** empowers the **President** to proclaim a **Financial Emergency** if he is satisfied that a situation has arisen whereby the financial stability or credit of India or any part of its territory is threatened.
 
• Although India faced a severe **economic crisis** in **1991** related to the **balance of payments**, a **Financial Emergency** was not declared.
 
• To date, the **Government of India** has **never** invoked **Article 360**; therefore, a **Financial Emergency** has never been proclaimed in the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Emergency (Article 352)**:

 
 
• It is proclaimed on grounds of **war**, **external aggression**, or **armed rebellion**.
 
• In India, it has been proclaimed **three times**: in **1962** (Indo-China war), **1971** (Indo-Pak war), and **1975** (internal disturbance).
 
• The **44th Amendment Act of 1978** replaced the term 'internal disturbance' with '**armed rebellion**'.
 
 
 
• **President's Rule (Article 356)**:
 
 
• Also known as **State Emergency** or **Constitutional Emergency**, it is imposed when a State Government cannot be carried on in accordance with the **Constitution**.
 
• This has been proclaimed **numerous times** (more than 100 instances) across various states since **1950**.
 
• **Punjab** was the first state where **President's Rule** was imposed in **1951**.
 
 
 
• **Approval and Duration**:
 
 
• A **National Emergency** must be approved by **Parliament** within **one month**, whereas **President's Rule** and **Financial Emergency** must be approved within **two months**.
 
• Once approved, **Financial Emergency** continues indefinitely until it is revoked by the **President**.

questions.question: Who has the power to appoint the Advocate General of a State?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Governor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to **Article 165** of the **Constitution of India**, the **Governor** of each state has the authority to appoint the **Advocate General** for the State.
 
• To be eligible for the appointment, the person must be qualified to be appointed as a **Judge of a High Court**, which requires being a **citizen of India** and having held a **judicial office** for ten years or served as an **advocate** in a High Court for at least ten years.
 
• The **Advocate General** serves as the **highest law officer** of the state government, providing legal advice and representing the state in legal matters assigned by the **Governor**.
 
• The Constitution does not provide a fixed tenure for the **Advocate General**; the official holds office during the **pleasure of the Governor** and receives remuneration as determined by the **Governor**.
 
• Conventionally, the **Advocate General** resigns when the **Council of Ministers** (government) resigns or is replaced, as they are appointed on its advice.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **President**:

 
 
• The **President of India** is responsible for appointing the **Attorney General of India** under **Article 76**, who is the corresponding highest law officer at the central level.
 
 
 
• **Chief Minister**:
 
 
• The **Governor** exercises the power of appointment based on the aid and advice of the **Council of Ministers**, which is headed by the **Chief Minister**.
 
 
 
• **State Legislature**:
 
 
• While the **State Legislature** does not appoint the **Advocate General**, the official has the right to speak and take part in the proceedings of the **Legislative Assembly** and **Legislative Council** (under **Article 177**) without the **right to vote**.

questions.question: What is the frequency range of sound that can be heard by the human ear?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**20 Hz to 20,000 Hz**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The human ear is sensitive to sound waves within a specific frequency range, typically spanning from **20 Hz** to **20,000 Hz** (or 20 kHz).
 
• **Frequency** is defined as the number of vibrations or cycles per second, and its **SI unit** is the **Hertz (Hz)**.
 
• Sound waves are **longitudinal mechanical waves** that require a medium (solid, liquid, or gas) to travel; they cannot propagate through a **vacuum**.
 
• The human ear is most sensitive to frequencies between **2,000 Hz** and **5,000 Hz**, which is the range where most human speech and communication occur.
 
• The anatomy of the ear, specifically the **tympanic membrane** (eardrum) and the **cochlea**, is biologically tuned to process vibrations within this specific audible spectrum.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Infrasonic Sound**:

 
 
• Refers to sounds with frequencies below **20 Hz**, which are too low for the human ear to perceive.
 
• These waves are produced by large-scale phenomena such as **earthquakes**, **volcanic eruptions**, and **ocean waves**.
 
• Certain animals like **elephants**, **hippos**, and **whales** utilize infrasound for long-distance communication.
 
 
 
• **Ultrasonic Sound**:
 
 
• Refers to sounds with frequencies exceeding **20,000 Hz**, which are beyond the upper limit of human hearing.
 
• Used extensively in medical **ultrasonography** (sonography) for imaging internal organs and in industrial applications like non-destructive testing.
 
• Animals such as **bats**, **dolphins**, and **porpoises** use ultrasound for **echolocation** to navigate and hunt in the dark or underwater.
 
 
 
• **Hearing Variations**:
 
 
• The upper limit of hearing typically decreases with age, a physiological phenomenon known as **presbycusis**.
 
• Children can often hear frequencies slightly above **20,000 Hz**, whereas elderly adults may have a restricted range ending at **12,000 Hz** or lower.

questions.question: Which of the following is the largest contributor to urban PM2.5 in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vehicle exhaust**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **PM2.5** refers to atmospheric particulate matter with a diameter of less than **2.5 micrometers**, which is small enough to enter the bloodstream and cause severe cardiovascular and respiratory diseases.
 
• In urban India, the **transportation sector** (vehicle exhaust) is consistently identified as the **largest primary contributor** to PM2.5 levels. Source apportionment studies by **IIT Kanpur** and the **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)** indicate that vehicles contribute between **28% and 47%** of the total PM2.5 load in major cities like **Delhi** and **Mumbai**.
 
• **Vehicle exhaust** is particularly critical because it releases pollutants at the **ground level**, leading to higher human exposure compared to industrial stacks which disperse pollutants at greater heights.
 
• While **Construction dust** is a significant source of coarser particles (PM10), its relative contribution to the finer **PM2.5** fraction is typically lower than that of combustion-related sources.
 
• **Industrial emissions** are major contributors in specific industrial zones, but on a city-wide average for residential and commercial **urban areas**, the sheer volume of **diesel and petrol vehicles** makes exhaust the dominant source.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Industrial emissions**:

 
 
• These involve pollutants from **power plants** and manufacturing units, primarily contributing **sulfur dioxide (SO2)** and nitrogen oxides, which can form **secondary PM2.5** in the atmosphere.
 
 
 
• **Construction dust**:
 
 
• Comprises crustal materials like **silica** and cement particles; while it adds to the **dust load**, it is generally easier to mitigate through **water sprinkling** and green barriers compared to chemical exhausts.
 
 
 
• **National Clean Air Programme (NCAP)**:
 
 
• Launched in **2019**, this initiative aims for a **20% to 30% reduction** in PM2.5 and PM10 concentrations by **2024** across 131 non-attainment cities in India.
 
 
 
• **Bharat Stage VI (BS-VI)**:
 
 
• India skipped **BS-V** and transitioned directly to **BS-VI** norms on **April 1, 2020**, to drastically reduce particulate matter and nitrogen oxide emissions from **new vehicles**.

questions.question: Which of the following meteorological factors can reduce Air Quality Index (AQI) temporarily?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rain**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rain** or **precipitation** acts as a natural air purifier through a process known as **wet deposition**. It is the most effective meteorological mechanism for the temporary removal of pollutants from the atmosphere.
 
• As raindrops fall, they collide with and capture suspended **particulate matter** (including **PM10** and **PM2.5**) through mechanical processes such as **impaction**, **diffusion**, and **interception**. This is technically referred to as **below-cloud scavenging** or **washout**.
 
• Rain also facilitates the removal of soluble gaseous pollutants like **sulfur dioxide (SO2)** and **nitrogen dioxide (NO2)** by dissolving them into water droplets, which then reach the ground.
 
• The physical removal of these contaminants leads to a rapid decrease in the concentration of pollutants in the immediate breathing zone, resulting in a significantly lower **Air Quality Index (AQI)** reading.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Temperature Inversion**:

 
 
• This phenomenon occurs when a layer of warm air sits above a layer of cooler air near the surface, reversing the normal **lapse rate**.
 
• It acts as a **lid** or **atmospheric cap**, preventing **vertical mixing** and trapping pollutants close to the ground, which drastically increases **AQI** levels.
 
 
 
• **Calm Wind**:
 
 
• Wind is essential for the **horizontal dispersion** and dilution of air pollutants.
 
• Stagnant or **calm wind** conditions allow pollutants to accumulate in one area, leading to high concentrations of **carbon monoxide (CO)** and other vehicular emissions.
 
 
 
• **High Humidity without Rain**:
 
 
• Moisture can lead to **hygroscopic growth**, where particles absorb water and expand, reducing visibility and potentially forming **secondary aerosols**.
 
• Without actual precipitation to wash the particles away, high humidity often worsens the **haze** and maintains high **PM** levels.

questions.question: Neeraj Chopra won his first-ever gold medal in javelin at the Asian Games in which year and city?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2018, Jakarta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Neeraj Chopra** scripted history by winning his first-ever **Asian Games gold medal** in the men's javelin throw event during the **2018 Asian Games**, which were co-hosted by **Jakarta** and **Palembang** in **Indonesia**.
 
• The final event took place on **August 27, 2018**, at the **Gelora Bung Karno Main Stadium**, where he delivered a powerful performance.
 
• He achieved the gold medal with a throw of **88.06 meters**, which set a new **National Record** for India at that time and was nearly six meters ahead of the silver medalist.
 
• This victory made him the first **Indian javelin thrower** to ever win a gold medal in the history of the **Asian Games**, cementing his status as a world-class athlete.
 
• His triumph in **Jakarta** followed a string of successes, including gold medals at the **2018 Commonwealth Games** in **Gold Coast** and the **2017 Asian Athletics Championships**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Major Career Achievements**:

 
 
• **Tokyo 2020 Olympics**: He became the first **Indian track and field athlete** to win an individual **Olympic gold medal** with a throw of **87.58 meters** in **2021**.
 
• **2022 Asian Games (Hangzhou)**: He successfully defended his title at the **19th Asian Games** in **China** (held in **2023**) by winning gold with a season-best throw of **88.88 meters**.
 
• **World Athletics Championships**: **Neeraj Chopra** won the gold medal at the **2023 Budapest World Championships** and a silver medal at the **2022 Eugene World Championships**.
 
• **Diamond League**: In **2022**, he became the first Indian to win the **Diamond League Trophy** at the final held in **Zurich**.
 
• **World Ranking**: He achieved the **World Number 1** ranking in the **Men's Javelin Throw** category as per **World Athletics** in **May 2023**.
 
• **Awards**: For his extraordinary contributions to sports, he was conferred with the **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna** in **2021** and the **Padma Shri**, India's fourth-highest civilian award, in **2022**.

questions.question: What are anabolic steroids primarily used for by athletes who misuse them?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Build muscle mass**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Anabolic-androgenic steroids (AAS)** are synthetic derivatives of the naturally occurring male hormone **testosterone**. The term **anabolic** specifically refers to the process of building up metabolic tissue, while **androgenic** refers to the development of male sexual characteristics.
 
• The primary mechanism through which these substances work is by binding to **androgen receptors** within muscle cells. This activation stimulates **protein synthesis** and promotes **nitrogen retention** in the muscles, which are critical components for **hypertrophy** (increased muscle size).
 
• Athletes and bodybuilders misuse these drugs to achieve a rate of muscle growth and physical strength that far exceeds what is naturally attainable through diet and exercise alone. This allows for a more significant **lean body mass** and enhanced physical appearance. Hence, the statement **Build muscle mass** is correct.
 
• Beyond simple growth, anabolic steroids help in the production of **adenosine triphosphate (ATP)** and promote the expansion of **satellite cells**, which are essential for repairing and thickening muscle fibers after high-intensity training sessions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Analysis of Other Functional Effects:**

 
 
• **Increase endurance:** While some steroids may slightly improve recovery, endurance is primarily enhanced through **Erythropoietin (EPO)** or blood doping, which increases **red blood cell count** and oxygen-carrying capacity.
 
• **Enhance flexibility:** Steroids do not improve flexibility; in fact, excessive muscle bulk and the tightening of tendons can sometimes lead to a **decreased range of motion**.
 
• **Reduce fatigue:** Although steroids allow for faster recovery between workouts by reducing **muscle damage** and inflammation, they are not classified as stimulants or fatigue-reducing agents like **caffeine** or **amphetamines**.
 
 
 
• **Health Risks of Misuse:**
 
 
• Cardiovascular issues such as **hypertension**, increased **LDL cholesterol**, and risk of heart attacks.
 
• Hormonal imbalances leading to **gynecomastia** in men and **virilization** (masculinization) in women.
 
• Potential for **liver damage** (hepatotoxicity), especially with oral formulations, and psychological effects often referred to as **roid rage**.

questions.question: Which element is required by the thyroid gland to produce thyroxine?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Iodine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **thyroid gland**, a butterfly-shaped endocrine organ located in the neck, requires **Iodine** to synthesize its primary hormones, **Thyroxine (T4)** and **Triiodothyronine (T3)**.
 
• **Iodine** is a trace element that is sequestered from the bloodstream by the thyroid follicular cells; the number '4' in **Thyroxine** specifically refers to the four atoms of iodine attached to the molecular structure.
 
• The primary function of **thyroxine** is to regulate the body's **basal metabolic rate (BMR)**, which controls how efficiently the body transforms nutrients into energy.
 
• In the absence of sufficient **Iodine**, the thyroid gland cannot produce enough hormones, causing a feedback loop where the **Pituitary Gland** overstimulates the thyroid, often resulting in an enlargement known as a **Goiter**.
 
• Dietary sources of **Iodine** include **iodized salt**, seafood, dairy products, and certain vegetables grown in iodine-rich soil, making it essential for preventing **hypothyroidism**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Calcium**

 
 
• It is the most abundant mineral in the body, primarily stored in **bones and teeth** to provide structural support.
 
• It is vital for **nerve transmission**, muscle contraction, and the activation of **blood clotting** factors.
 
 
 
• **Sodium**
 
 
• It is the principal cation in the **extracellular fluid**, playing a dominant role in maintaining **osmotic pressure** and fluid balance.
 
• It is essential for the conduction of **nerve impulses** and the transport of nutrients like glucose across cell membranes.
 
 
 
• **Potassium**
 
 
• It acts as the main intracellular cation and is critical for maintaining **resting membrane potential** in neurons and muscle cells.
 
• Proper levels are necessary to regulate **heartbeat** and prevent cardiac arrhythmias.

questions.question: The Goods and Services Tax Council is chaired by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Finance Minister of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Goods and Services Tax (GST) Council** is a constitutional body established under **Article 279A** of the Indian Constitution, which was inserted by the **101st Amendment Act, 2016**.
 
• The Council is chaired by the **Union Finance Minister**, who acts as the ex-officio head. Currently, this position is held by **Nirmala Sitharaman**.
 
• It serves as a joint forum between the **Union** and the **States** to make recommendations on complex issues related to **GST**, including tax rates, **exemptions**, threshold limits, and **dispute resolution**.
 
• The **Union Minister of State** in charge of **Revenue or Finance** serves as a member, along with **Ministers** in charge of Finance or Taxation nominated by each **State Government**.
 
• The **GST Council** ensures a harmonized structure of **indirect taxation** across the country, embodying the principle of **Cooperative Federalism**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prime Minister**:

 
 
• The **Prime Minister** serves as the head of the **Union Council of Ministers** and chairs bodies like the **NITI Aayog** and the **National Selection Committee**.
 
• While the Prime Minister oversees the overall economic vision, they do not participate in the day-to-day administrative meetings or the chairing of the **GST Council**.
 
 
 
• **RBI Governor**:
 
 
• The **Governor of the Reserve Bank of India** chairs the **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)** and is responsible for managing **inflation** and **liquidity**.
 
• The RBI is a **regulatory body** for the banking sector and does not have a voting or chairing role in **fiscal policy** bodies like the GST Council.
 
 
 
• **NITI Aayog CEO**:
 
 
• The **Chief Executive Officer** of NITI Aayog is a high-ranking civil servant who manages the administrative affairs of the **National Institution for Transforming India**.
 
• The CEO provides **strategic inputs** for long-term policy but does not hold a constitutional chair in the tax council.
 
 
 
• **Voting Mechanism**:
 
 
• Decisions in the **GST Council** are taken by a majority of not less than **three-fourths** (75%) of the weighted votes.
 
• The **Central Government** holds **one-third** (33.33%) of the total weightage, while the **State Governments** combined hold **two-thirds** (66.67%) of the total weightage of votes cast.

questions.question:
Which of the following is a target groups for PM-DAKSH Scheme which is seen in news in July 2025?

I. Scheduled Caste

II. Other Backward Caste
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Pradhan Mantri Dakshata Aur Kushalata Sampann Hitgrahi** (PM-DAKSH) Yojana is a **Central Sector Scheme** launched by the **Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment** during **2020-21** to provide high-quality **skill development** training.
 
• The scheme focuses on the **Scheduled Caste** (SC) population as a primary target group, aiming to enhance their competency levels to make them employable in both **self-employment** and **wage-employment** sectors for socio-economic upliftment. ***Hence, statement I is correct.***
 
• The **Other Backward Classes** (OBCs) are also a designated target group under the scheme, specifically those individuals whose **annual family income** is less than **3 Lakh**. ***Hence, statement II is correct.***
 
• The implementation of the training programs is carried out through three **Apex Corporations**: National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (**NSFDC**), National Backward Classes Finance & Development Corporation (**NBCFDC**), and National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (**NSKFDC**).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Target Group Diversity**:

 
 
• **Economically Backward Classes** (EBCs): Individuals from families with an annual income below **1 Lakh** are eligible for training.
 
• **De-notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes** (DNTs): Members of these marginalized communities are included without any specific income ceiling.
 
• **Safai Karamcharis**: This includes **waste pickers** and their dependents, focusing on their **rehabilitation** through **vocational training**.
 
 
 
• **Training Categories**:
 
 
• **Up-skilling/Reskilling**: Aimed at traditional artisans and workers to improve their efficiency and income.
 
• **Short Term Training**: Programs lasting 200 to 600 hours aligned with **National Skill Qualification Framework** (NSQF) levels.
 
• **Entrepreneurship Development Programme** (EDP): Specific 10 to 15-day training for those interested in starting their own business ventures.
 
• **Long Term Training**: Comprehensive training for 6 months to 1 year in high-demand sectors like **healthcare** and **information technology**.

questions.question: 'Kambala' festival is celebrated in which of the following Indian state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Karnataka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kambala** is a traditional **buffalo race** held annually in the coastal districts of **Karnataka**, specifically in **Dakshina Kannada** and **Udupi**.
 
• The festival is deeply rooted in the agrarian culture of the **Tuluva community** and is typically held between **November** and **March**.
 
• The race takes place in **slushy paddy fields** (called Kambala gadde) where pairs of buffaloes are driven by a whip-lashing farmer across the mud and water.
 
• Historically, the event was organized to propitiate **Lord Kadri Manjunatha** (an incarnation of **Lord Shiva**) to ensure a good harvest and protect livestock from diseases.
 
• To protect this cultural heritage against legal challenges regarding animal welfare, the **Karnataka Government** passed the **Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (Karnataka Amendment) Bill, 2017**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gujarat**:

 
 
• Famous for the **International Kite Festival (Uttarayan)** held in **Ahmedabad** during **January**.
 
• The state is also the heart of **Navratri** celebrations, featuring the **Garba** dance dedicated to Goddess **Durga**.
 
 
 
• **Assam**:
 
 
• Renowned for **Bihu**, which consists of three distinct festivals: **Rongali Bihu** (Spring), **Kongali Bihu** (Autumn), and **Bhogali Bihu** (Harvest).
 
• Host to the **Ambubachi Mela** at the **Kamakhya Temple** in **Guwahati**.
 
 
 
• **Tripura**:
 
 
• Celebrates **Kharchi Puja**, a major festival where **14 deities** are worshipped over seven days in **Agartala**.
 
• Also known for **Garia Puja**, a traditional festival celebrated by tribal communities to seek blessings for prosperity.

questions.question: Who delivered a speech in Bombay on January 15, 1908, declaring that the purpose of national education was to awaken the spirit of nationalism among students?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sri Aurobindo Ghose**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On **January 15, 1908**, **Sri Aurobindo Ghose** delivered a historic speech in **Bombay** (now Mumbai) regarding the necessity and philosophy of **National Education**.
 
• In this address, he explicitly declared that the primary purpose of national education was to **awaken the spirit of nationalism** among students, urging them to dedicate their lives to the service of the motherland.
 
• The speech was delivered shortly after the **Surat Split** of the **Indian National Congress** (1907), a period when **Aurobindo Ghose** emerged as a prominent leader of the **Extremist** faction, advocating for **Purna Swaraj** (complete independence).
 
• He criticized the colonial education system for being a 'factory for producing clerks' and argued that true education should be rooted in the **Indian soul**, culture, and traditions to foster mental and spiritual strength.
 
• **Aurobindo Ghose** was deeply involved in the practical implementation of these ideals, serving as the first **Principal** of the **Bengal National College**, which was established in **1906** as part of the **Swadeshi Movement**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Other Personalities and Education:**

 
 
• **Rabindranath Tagore:** Founded **Shantiniketan** in 1901 and later **Visva-Bharati University**; he focused on **naturalistic** and **aesthetic education**, emphasizing harmony between man and nature.
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi:** Proposed the **Wardha Scheme of Education** or **Nai Talim** (Basic Education) in **1937**, focusing on **handicrafts** and self-sufficiency; he was in **South Africa** in January 1908.
 
• **Lala Lajpat Rai:** A key leader from **Punjab** who was instrumental in the **Dayanand Anglo-Vedic (DAV)** school movement, promoting education based on **Vedic principles** and modern science.

questions.question: The ______ religious group saw the highest decadal population growth rate in India between the 2001 and 2011 censuses.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Muslim**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Census of India 2011**, the **Muslim** religious community recorded the highest decadal growth rate of **24.6%** during the period **2001−2011**.
 
• The **Hindu** population, which is the largest religious group, saw a growth rate of **16.8%**, while the national average for the same period was **17.7%**.
 
• Among other major religions, **Christians** grew by **15.5%**, **Sikhs** by **8.4%**, and **Buddhists** by **6.1%**.
 
• The **Jain** community registered the lowest growth rate at **5.4%** between the two census operations.
 
• While the **Muslim** growth rate remained the highest, it observed a significant decline from the **29.5%** growth rate recorded in the **1991−2001** decade.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Decadal Growth Rate**:

 
 
• It is the percentage change in the population of a specific area or group over a span of **ten years**.
 
• The **Census 2011** data revealed that the total population of India reached **121.09 crore**.
 
 
 
• **Hindu Religious Group**:
 
 
• Maintains the largest share of the Indian population at **79.8%** (approximately **96.63 crore**).
 
• The growth rate dropped from **19.92%** in the previous decade to **16.76%** in 2011.
 
 
 
• **Sikh and Buddhist Groups**:
 
 
• The **Sikh** population stood at **2.08 crore**, making up **1.7%** of the total population in 2011.
 
• The **Buddhist** population was recorded at **0.84 crore**, accounting for **0.7%** of the total population.
 
 
 
• **Muslim Population Share**:
 
 
• The proportion of **Muslims** in the total population increased from **13.4%** in 2001 to **14.2%** in 2011.

questions.question: The Operation Gideon Chariots is associated with which of the following country?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Israel**__.

***__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Operation Gideon's Chariots** (Hebrew: Mivtza Markavot Gid'on*) is a military offensive launched by the **Israel Defense Forces (IDF)** in the **Gaza Strip**.
 
• The operation was approved by the Israeli security cabinet in May **2025** and officially commenced on May 16, **2025**.
 
• Its stated primary objectives include the dismantling of **Hamas**'s military and administrative infrastructure, neutralizing its underground tunnel networks, and securing the release of hostages.
 
• The comprehensive ground, air, and sea offensive involved major active military formations, including the **98th, 36th, 162nd, 252nd, and Gaza divisions**.
 
• A follow-up phase of the campaign, named **Operation Gideon's Chariots II** (or Chariots of Gideon B), was approved by Defense Minister **Israel Katz** in August **2025** to sustain pressure on militant groups in **Gaza City**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Other Historic Operations by Israel:**

 
 
• **Operation Swords of Iron:** Initiated following the coordinated cross-border attacks on October 7, **2023**.
 
• **Operation Protective Edge (2014):** Launched with the aim of destroying cross-border assault tunnels.
 
• **Operation Cast Lead (2008−2009):** A three-week armed conflict aimed at stopping rocket fire into Israeli territory.
 
 
 
• **The Gaza Strip:**
 
 
• It is a narrow coastal enclave located on the eastern coast of the **Mediterranean Sea**.
 
• It shares land borders with **Egypt** to the southwest and **Israel** to the north and east.
